title: Why Microwaves Heat Soup But Never the Bowl

scenes.narration: A microwave oven doesn't heat food from the outside in. It targets water molecules directly using electromagnetic resonance.
scenes.objective: Show the closed microwave then reveal the hidden magnetron and waveguide

scenes.narration: Inside the wall sits a magnetron vacuum tube firing waves at two point four five gigahertz.
scenes.objective: Reveal magnetron cutaway with electrons spiraling in resonant vanes

scenes.narration: Water molecules are electric dipoles, positively charged on hydrogen, negatively charged on oxygen.
scenes.objective: Macro view of water molecule dipole aligning with oscillating field
scenes.note: Illustrative - molecule enlarged 1000000x, field oscillation slowed

scenes.narration: As the field flips billions of times per second, molecules twist violently, turning friction into boiling heat.
scenes.objective: Show soup heating with molecular chaos and steam rising
scenes.note: Illustrative - molecular motion slowed, steam exaggerated

scenes.narration: Glass and ceramic bowls lack free dipoles, so the radiation passes straight through without warming them.
scenes.objective: Show waves passing through bowl material while water absorbs

scenes.narration: The oven doesn't cook your food. It forces the water inside your food to boil itself.
scenes.objective: Final reveal of complete system working together
